$\,1.3\,$ $0.9049$ $0.9066$ $0.9082$
$\,1.4\,$ $0.9207$ $0.9222$ $0.9236$

$\,2.8\,$ $0.9974$ $0.9975$ $0.9976$

question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-1$ and $\sigma =\sqrt{4}=2.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.64<X<4.4) & =P(\frac{1.64-(-1)}{2}<Z<\frac{4.4-(-1)}{2}) \\  & =P(1.32<Z<2.7)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/5f9157c11ed6b5548663ac376a3e4ff8137e8c4d0ba418dffdc19f7aa89914d3.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.32<Z<2.7) & =P(Z<2.7)-P(Z\le 1.32) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.7)-P(Z\le 1.32) \\  & =Φ(2.7)-Φ(1.32)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.32) & =0.9066 \\ Φ(2.7) & =0.9965\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.32<Z<2.7) & =Φ(2.7)-Φ(1.32) \\  & =0.9965-0.9066 \\  & =0.0899.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(1.64<X<4.4)=0.0899.
$$
